name: Home for Incurable and Infirm Women, The
title: Home for Incurable and Infirm Women, The
---

Mentioned 26 April 1864. This was run by [Louisa Twining](/person/1427), and operated from 21 Great Ormond Street. Twining described its work in an article in MP (April 1864) 437-449; and further in a letter MP (August 1869) 205-6. The latter gives the number of inmates as 27.

Some correspondence of the Charity Organization Society with an outfit of this name, running a home for respectable women in reduced circumstances at Whetstone, is held by the London Metropolitan Archives.
